title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from this and the neighbouring pages: S is a normal scheme of finite type over a field (say Q), with function field K. U → S is a relative (hyperbolic) curve with fibres U_s (compactified X_s). Here E_• denotes fundamental or Galois groups: E_K = Gal(K̄/K), E_{U_K} = π1(U_K), E_{X_s} = π1 of the fibre, E_{k(s)} = Gal(k(s)^sep/k(s)).

The preceding page reinterprets a rational section f of U/S, defined on an open S' ⊂ S, as the family of points f(s) ∈ U_s for s ∈ S'. This page translates that into the language of sections of group extensions:
- A Galois section ξ of E_{U_K} → E_K, the 'generic' anabelian datum, should give a family of 'neighbouring' sections of E_{X_s} → E_{k(s)} for s ∈ S'. This is exactly what a rational section of U/S does pointwise.
- To make the correspondence precise, he generalises what was done earlier when s has codimension 1 (S locally a trait):
  1. Take the normalisation S̄ of S in K̄.
  2. The fibre of S̄ over s is the set of maximal ideals of the integral closure of O_{S,s} in K̄.
  3. For a point s' over s, its stabiliser N_{s'} ⊂ Gal(K̄/K) is the decomposition group. It sits in an extension 1 → I_{s'} → N_{s'} → E_{k(s)} → 1, with I_{s'} the inertia group.
- The next page identifies I_{s'} with the absolute Galois group of the fraction field of the strict henselisation of O_{S,s}, and N_{s'} with that of the ordinary henselisation. It then argues as follows. If the composite E_K → E_{U_K} → E_U kills I_{s'}, which is the group-theoretic counterpart of 's ∈ S'', then the restriction of ξ to N_{s'} descends to a homomorphism E_{k(s)} → E_U. This factors through π1(U ×_S Spec O^h_{S,s}) ≅ π1(X_s), giving a section of E_{X_s} → E_{k(s)}, i.e. a 'specialisation' of ξ at s.
- The next page then turns to s ∉ S', where D = S∖S' is of pure codimension 1, using μ_d-torsors (Kummer theory).

Purpose: understand the section conjecture in families. One wants to relate Galois sections over a finitely generated field K to sections over residue fields k(s) of its specialisations, e.g. to pass between function fields and number fields, and to recognise sections coming from rational points of U/S.
errors: No real error. The identifications decomposition group ≅ Gal of Frac(O^h) and inertia ≅ Gal of Frac(O^sh) need O_{S,s} normal, so that its henselisation is a normal domain. Surjectivity N_{s'} → Gal(k(s)^sep/k(s)) is the standard result for normal local rings. Normality is implicit in his use of the normalisation.

The specialisation step needs a specialisation isomorphism π1(U_{O^h_s}) ≅ π1(U_s). For open curves this holds only for the prime-to-p, or tame, part in positive residue characteristic, and requires U/S to be a good (smooth, with étale divisor at infinity) relative curve near s. This is harmless over Q-varieties but is left implicit. The page also writes X_s where U_s is meant in places.
'Codimension 1' refers to the point s being of codimension 1 (local ring a DVR), not to S itself.

ideas.what: Decomposition group of a point s' of the normalisation of S in K̄ above a point s of arbitrary codimension, forming an extension 1 → I_{s'} → N_{s'} → Gal(k(s)) → 1. I and N are identified with the Galois groups of the fraction fields of the strict and ordinary henselisations of O_{S,s}.
ideas.modern_name: decomposition/inertia groups for normal local rings (higher-dimensional ramification theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hilbert/Krull for the general theory; henselisation version standard (Nagata, Raynaud, SGA 1/SGA 4)
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 (ramification, fundamental group of henselian local schemes), SGA 4 VIII (strict henselisation)

ideas.what: Specialising a Galois section of π1(U_K) → G_K at a point s: if the composite kills inertia, the section descends to a section of π1(U_s) → G_{k(s)}. This matches 'neighbouring' sections with the points f(s) of a rational section of U/S.
ideas.modern_name: specialisation of sections (section conjecture over finitely generated fields / in families)
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Stix (specialisation of sections; Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups, LNM 2054, 2013); also Pop, Esnault–Wittenberg, Saïdi in related forms
ideas.where_published: The section conjecture over finitely generated fields is in the letter to Faltings (1983); the specialisation mechanism is not, to my knowledge, worked out there

ideas.what: Group-theoretic characterisation of the domain of definition S' of the rational section: s ∈ S' iff E_K → E_U kills the inertia I_{s'}. Points outside S' are to be treated by Kummer (μ_d-torsor) arguments along the purely codimension-1 divisor D = S∖S'.
ideas.modern_name: inertia-triviality criterion for good reduction / extension of sections (purity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard purity (Zariski–Nagata, SGA 1 X); cuspidal-section analysis in Stix's book

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a dictionary between Galois sections over the function field K of a higher-dimensional base S and families of fibrewise Galois sections over all points s ∈ S, including higher codimension, via decomposition groups in Gal(K̄/K). He also starts treating the bad locus D = S∖S' via μ_d-torsors. This is a 'section conjecture in families' viewpoint predating Stix's specialisation results by ~25 years, but it is only sketched here.
missed.quote: on peut préciser ainsi cette correspondance [entre] sections de E_{U_K} sur E_K, et sections des E_{X_s} sur les E_{k(s)}, en généralisant ce qu'on a vu dans le cas où s est de codimension 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the specialisation-of-sections technique used to reduce the section conjecture from finitely generated fields to number fields. The mathematics itself is now in the literature (Stix), so novelty is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct sketch of specialisation of Galois sections via decomposition and inertia groups at points of arbitrary codimension. Interesting as an early (mid-1980s) unpublished appearance of a technique later developed by Stix and others, but the content is standard and now in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 reads roughly '... (où S est de type fini sur un corps, tel Q disons)'; the opening words of the page are illegible and 'Lerdinand' is surely a misreading.
'En termes de sections d'extensions [?]' rather than 'sections de catégories'.
'la section ξ_{K̄} de E_{U_K} sur E_K donne lieu à [?] ... : une famille de sections des E_{X_s} sur les E_{k(s)} pour s ∈ S''.
'On peut préciser ainsi cette correspondance entre sections de E_{U_K} sur E_K, et sections des E_{X_s} sur les E_{k(s)}' ('Une pour' is a misreading of 'On peut').
'dans le cas où s est de codimension 1': s, the point, not S.
'On introduit la normalisée S̄ de S dans K̄, la fibre en s s'identifie à l'ensemble des idéaux maximaux de la clôture normale de O_{S,s} dans K̄'.
'le stabilisateur dans E_K d'un s' dans S̄_s' (stabilisateur replacing struck 'normalisateur').
